A style describes the day. A destination gives it a place.

Explore the methods, boats and waters that suit you. Then choose from every matching catalog trip.

Looking for a local name? Explore 41 local classics ↗
104 MATCHING DESTINATIONS

Inshore & flats

Fish sheltered bays, estuaries, mangroves or shallow saltwater flats. The water and tide shape the day.

85 MATCHING DESTINATIONS

Offshore & bluewater

Travel beyond the sheltered coast to fish open water. Trolling, casting and other methods depend on the target.

15 MATCHING DESTINATIONS

Surf & pier

Fish from the beach, rocks or a pier. Access, casting space and surf conditions set the limits.

336 MATCHING DESTINATIONS

Fly fishing

Present a fly with a fly rod. This method spans small streams, large rivers and saltwater flats.

69 MATCHING DESTINATIONS

River float & drift boat

Cover a river reach from a moving boat. The launch, take-out and river level are part of the trip plan.

256 MATCHING DESTINATIONS

Lake & reservoir

Fish enclosed freshwater, from a large reservoir to a smaller lake. Depth, access and species determine the method.

13 MATCHING DESTINATIONS

Ice fishing

Fish through ice with a locally assessed access plan. A winter date alone does not establish safe ice.

35 MATCHING DESTINATIONS

Fly-in & remote lodge

Use a remote lodge or an air transfer as the base for a fishing trip. Travel and equipment limits shape the plan.

3 MATCHING DESTINATIONS

Kayak fishing

Fish from a small paddle or pedal craft. The route, launch and weather plan are as important as the tackle.

72 MATCHING DESTINATIONS

Bottom fishing & combo charters

Fish near the bottom for local targets, or combine supported fisheries in one boat day. A combo depends on time and conditions.

3 MATCHING DESTINATIONS

Night fishing

Fish after dark with a plan for visibility, access and the return. The method depends on the place and target.

10 MATCHING DESTINATIONS

Sight fishing

Locate a visible fish before the cast. Light, clarity and a careful approach are central to the method.

24 MATCHING DESTINATIONS

Big-game & billfish

Plan a boat trip around large pelagic fish such as billfish or tuna. The target and local method define the tackle.

5 MATCHING DESTINATIONS

Multi-species slams

Work toward a locally defined group of species in one trip. The meaning of a slam changes with the region.

402 MATCHING DESTINATIONS

Bank & wade

Reach the water from shore or by wading. Access rights, footing, depth and current set the practical limits.

309 MATCHING DESTINATIONS

River & stream

Fish flowing freshwater from the bank, by wading or from a boat. The reach and water level shape the day.
